newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dow rally lifts Europe bourses, dlr up on yen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dow rally lifts Europe bourses, dlr up on yen.

text.p: London, Frankfurt and Paris stocks were all boosted on Wednesday by an overnight Wall Street rally which propelled the Dow to a new record, while on currency markets the dollar touched an 11-week peak against the yen.

The dollar hit a high of 118.75 yen in early European trading after Japanese industrial output and retail sales data bolstered expectations that Japan's interest rates will stay near record lows for the time being.

By mid-morning in Europe, the U.S. currency was steady just below its peak against the yen, at around 118.60, but was unable to break above the 1.84 level against the mark amid speculation the Bundesbank could switch to using variable-rate tenders to set its securities repurchase rate.
London's FTSE 100 stock index opened in high spirits, taking its cue from the encouraging performance in New York, where the Dow finished 53.42 points higher at 8,174.53.
A firmer opening for the index futures fuelled initial gains, sending the index up 25 points or half a percentage point to 4,902 by 1000 GMT.

Dealers said the progress of sterling was likely to remain a focus after the currency's sharp slide on Tuesday gave a major boost to exporters. The pound bounced off lows overnight after falling nearly four percent so far this week.
One damper on the London market came from two major FTSE companies, BAT Industries and Guardian Royal Exchange, both of which reported half-year profits below the average of analysts' forecasts.
"These two FTSE companies will make an impact on us," one dealer said. "There's a lot of nervousness surrounding this interim results season and we are getting a good insight into current trading."
In Frankfurt German shares were heading for a new record high in morning bourse trade, catching up to early gains in pre-bourse IBIS computer dealings.
The overnight Wall Street gains and the firmer dollar -- seen as good for exports -- helped support German stocks but dealers said profit-taking could emerge as the market moves up.
The 30-share DAX was up 31.7 points at 4,413.39 points at 0930 GMT. The DAX record high stood at 4,418.64 points, set on July 23.
It was a similar story on the Paris bourse, which opened at a fresh all-time high, also supported by Wall Street and the firm dollar.
The main CAC-40 index was up 1.1 percent at 3057.1 at 0930 GMT. The previous record of 3044.24 was established on Monday.
Pharmaceutical and beauty products group Sanofi continued its strong rise from Tuesday on expectations it will sell its 49.9 percent stake in the Nina Ricci perfume business.

In the currency markets, talk of developments in German rates was kept alive by comments Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick made in an interview with Germany's Handelsblatt newspaper. He said the Bundesbank had to balance a weak economy against a weak mark.

Koebnick added that the German central bank had made provision for sending a rate signal before its summer break. It fixed the repo rate at 3.0 percent for two weeks rather than the usual four weeks before its summer recess.
Traders were expecting the dollar to claw back ground it lost to the mark on Tuesday after its surge to a seven-and-a-half-year peak of 1.8490 on Monday triggered profit taking.
"We tend to go up by the stairs and down by the lift these days but there is good demand for dollars after yesterday's correction and we should grind higher," said a trader in London.

Meanwhile, on the London metal exchange, zinc prices were recovering after their headlong plunge on Tuesday. LME benchmark three-month zinc dropped 300 dollars per tonne to a low of 1,370 dollars on Tuesday as speculators scambled to liquidate their positions. But by mid-morning Wednesday what dealers described as residual tightness had pulled three-month zinc back to above 1,500 dollars.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8395 marks and 118.60 yen compared with 1.8299 and 117.82 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 25.6 points at 4,902.2.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was up 31.7 points in bourse trade at 4,413.39.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 33.35 points at 3,057.1.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $326.40 compared with London's close on Tuesday of 326.45. Silver was also quiet at $4.35, up four cents.
